text: By this point you know how to build a technically sound catalog — scan for technical metadata, curate business context, link to the glossary and dictionary, make it searchable. None of that guarantees anyone actually uses it.
Adoption is a separate, harder problem — and it's the one that determines whether all the work in this course pays off or sits unused.

Three barriers sink well-built catalogs. Habit — people already have a working method that's faster for them right now. Trust — one stale or wrong search result, and they conclude the catalog isn't reliable, often permanently. Visibility — a catalog nobody knows exists gets zero adoption regardless of quality.

For habit: integrate the catalog into existing workflows, a search widget embedded in the BI tool people already open, not a separate destination. For trust: launch with a smaller, genuinely high-quality scope — a hundred reliable entries beat a thousand of mixed quality. For visibility: actively announce it where people already look, not passive publishing.

Most failed metadata programs aren't failed because the technology was wrong — they're failed because nobody treated adoption as its own deliberate workstream. Next lesson: a metadata case study, pulling all five chapters together, end to end.
